column3: “Atharim” is treated as a place name; the word may also mean “the spies,” so the meaning is uncertain.
“indeed” renders an emphatic doubled verb, and “utterly destroy” renders “devote to destruction (haram)” (also in verse 3).
“the Red Sea” renders “Sea of Reeds,” and “became impatient” renders “their soul became short.”
“we loathe” renders “our soul loathes,” and “this miserable food” renders “this worthless (qeloqel) food.”
“fiery serpents” renders “the serpents, the seraphim (burning ones).”
“opposite Moab” renders “on the face of Moab,” and “to the east” renders “toward the sunrise.”
The quotation “Waheb in Suphah” is obscure in the Hebrew; the meaning is uncertain.
“the site of Ar” renders “the dwelling of Ar.”
“sank” renders “dug,” and “the scepter” renders “mehoqeq,” a ruler’s staff.
“the king’s highway” renders “the way of the king.”
“the edge of the sword” renders “the mouth of the sword”; NASB reads “the border … was Jazer,” where the Hebrew has “the border … was strong (az).”
“those who use proverbs” renders “the moshelim (speakers of sayings).”
“The dominant heights” renders “the lords (ba’ale) of the high places.”
“we have cast them down” renders a verb that may mean “we shot at them”; the verse is difficult, and the meaning is uncertain.
